collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A friend asks a villager what they would tell a friend with their own problem: answer, or refuse to play along.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is going round and round about whether to tell (subject.his/her) work crew that (subject.he/she) wants a different job. (friend) listens for a while, then says, "Imagine I came to you with this exact problem. What would you tell me?"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) thinks about it. "I'd tell you to say something. Kindly. That you'd rather do something else and it's not their fault." (friend) waits. (subject) sighs. "Alright. Alright, I hear it." (subject.He/she) talks to the crew the next day. It goes fine. Not perfect, but fine. Later (subject.he/she) tries the same trick on (friend), who finds it extremely annoying.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "That doesn't work on me," says (subject). "I'm much nicer to other people than to myself." (friend) laughs. "Then be nicer to yourself." "I'll think about it," says (subject). (subject.He/she) doesn't decide anything that night. But walking home, (subject.he/she) hears (subject.him/her)self thinking, "I'd tell a friend it's alright to want something different." It sticks.
